newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine's PNB to build capital, sell more assets.
newsitem.headline: Philippine's PNB to build capital, sell more assets.

text.p: The Philippine National Bank (PNB) plans to build up capital to cope with growing competition in the country's banking industry, PNB president Peter Favila said on Tuesday.

"We need to have a continuing build-up of our capital base," Favila told reporters after shareholders approved a resolution increasing the bank's authorised capital to 25 billion pesos from 10 billion pesos.

The PNB, once the country's biggest bank, has been battered by competition in the past few years due to its limited resources. It slipped from its leading position in the early 1990s following a rise in the number of new domestic banks.
The bank no longer needs congressional approval before raising capital after a privatisation last year trimmed the government's stake in PNB to 47.3 percent.
Favila said he had drawn up four strategies for the bank to build its capital base. The measures, which he declined to state, were still being studied by the government, he added.
He did not discount the possibility of a merger with another bank.
"I am open to a merger... as long as they approach us, we are willing to talk to them," Favila said.
In the meantime, the bank plans to continue selling its idle assets, which are mostly land, to help finance its expansion.
The bank booked extraordinary income of 3.790 billion pesos ($144 milion) in the first nine months of this year from the sale of its assets.
At present, the bank has more than 3.0 billion pesos ($114 million) worth of idle properties that will be disposed of in the coming years.
Leading the list of properties to be offered on the auction block is a 2.5 hectare bayfront property which was valued at 65,000 pesos ($2,475) per square metre last year.
The bank's headquarters, which has 15.5 hectares of floor space, will be leased to interested parties.
Foremost in the bank's expansion programme is the information technology network.
"I admit we are not very advanced in our information technology, but we are fast-tracking our integrated banking solution by next year," Favila said.
The phasing in of the technology network would be in tandem with the restructuring of the bank's staffing.
Currently, the bank has about 7,600 workers in its 303 branches nationwide. It had retired 500 workers in the past six months and was planning to cut staff strength further.

Favila declined to give specific numbers on further staffing cuts, but said an independent consultancy company is currently working on the numbers. A study is expected to be finalised in two weeks' time.

PNB is also set to sell 60 percent of its losing banking subsidiary, PNB-Republic Bank, to other banks by the middle of the month. Among the interested buyers are Malayan Banking Bhd and National Australia Bank, Favila added.
